verdict.rationale: Google Cloud's own IAM provides fine-grained control over who can do what on which resource. Workload Identity Federation lets workloads reach Google Cloud resources through federated identities instead of service account keys. Together these are a first-party basis for least-privilege credentials, but the evidence never shows issuing a scoped credential for an agent. Missing for 10: explicit docs on creating scoped service accounts or short-lived tokens for agents, agent-specific credential guidance, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: IAM est un outil permettant de gérer les autorisations précises pour Google Cloud.
IAM memungkinkan Anda mengontrol _siapa_ yang dapat melakukan _apa_ pada _resource mana_.
Using Workload Identity Federation, you can provide on-premises or multicloud workloads with access to Google Cloud resources by using federated identities instead of a service account key.
